newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nedcor sees scope for two SAfrica rate cuts.
newsitem.headline: Nedcor sees scope for two SAfrica rate cuts.

text.p: South African interest rates could be reduced in September and then again in December or January, banking group Nedcor Ltd said on Thursday.

"We still believe that we are likely to get a cut in rates in September and then possibly another one in December/January," Nedcor chief executive Richard Laubscher said at the group's interim results presentation.

"I think the lead to that is occuring in the money markets already. The money markets are showing a slightly softer tone," Laubscher said. But he added that the rate reduction outlook had become less certain.
Private credit in South Africa was falling while corporate credit was growing, Laubscher said.
"There is no doubt that consumer credit is declining and there is no doubt that corporate credit is advancing for very good reasons," he said.
The advance in corporate credit was partly due to the economy opening up after the democratic elections in 1994 and corporations now replacing offshore borrowing with local borrowing, he said.
A growing number of investment projects also demanded more funding, he said.

"The number of projects on the go by major corporates is amazing and some of that is now translating through into increased medium term borrowing Demand. We've been pretty fortunate in that we've financed some of the more high profile projects," Laubscher said.
